messages.subject: Setting bounds unexpectedly influencing estimates
parts:
Dear All,
I estimated a parameter in one model that represents a correlation and should be bound between -1 and +1. I included an inequality constraint like p > -1 ; p <1 (maybe there is another way to impose bounds on parameters?)
The parameter seems to hit the low bound as it returns as -1. However, when I took out the constraint, the parameter was estimated to 0.15,  (and all other parameters in the model where sometimes largely different). THis did not make sense to me as the parameter was WITHIN the bounds and should not have been affected. Someone checked the same model in OpenMx for me; The parameter was estimated to 0.15  when including bounds or not. So there was sth weird going on. Unfortunately, I can't share the data and the model is complex. It does not matter for me right now as I'm putting this model aside anyway. However, I wanted to signal this in case anyone has an idea of what was going or a reproducible example of this issue.
Many Thanks!
JB

messages.subject: RE: Setting bounds unexpectedly influencing estimates
parts:
A tool to graph the estimated value of a parameter across iterations would be really useful in some diagnostic situations.  This sounds like a case where the estimate goes out of bounds but comes back.  Different starting values might alter this behavior, and OpenMx may use different starting values.  Setting starting values in lavaan might eliminate the behavior.

--Ed Rigdon

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Setting bounds unexpectedly influencing estimates
parts:
On 03/22/2014 07:27 PM, JB wrote:
> Dear All,
> I estimated a parameter in one model that represents a correlation and
> should be bound between -1 and +1. I included an inequality constraint
> like p > -1 ; p <1

It would help more if we could see the R script. In lavaan, a free
parameter can never be a correlation! It is always a covariance.

[It is possible to define correlations based on estimated covariances by
using the := operator, and scale appropriately, but I don't think this
is what you have done.]

So we are left with the suggestion that lavaan is doing something wrong,
but without evidence...

Yves
